📸 Inauguración del Hospital General IMSS Bienestar — Ciudad Madero, Tamaulipas, 16 de agosto de 2026

🏥✊ "Here, care doesn't depend on an affiliation or any ability to pay. No fees, no copays, no conditions of any kind." — Alejandro Svarch, IMSS Bienestar director, Ciudad Madero 538,000 people in the region have no social security. Over 1 billion pesos went into rescuing the hospital: 179 beds (up from under 100), 5 operating rooms (from 2), 20 specialties, the best CT scanner in the region, 100+ new doctors and nurses — and a fully digital clinical control center, a first for Mexico's public health system.

🇲🇽📊 "From 1943 to 1982, 29,000 hospital beds were built. In the next 36 years, only 4,000." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Ciudad Madero, Tamaulipas Sheinbaum's arithmetic on six neoliberal administrations (1982-2018): as population and chronic disease grew, public hospital construction collapsed while private clinics boomed. Her count: 80 abandoned hospitals inherited in 2018 — including this one, started in 2015 and left as a shell.

🏥🇲🇽 "The goal: free healthcare for every Mexican — medicines in every clinic and hospital, doctors, nurses. That's where we're headed." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Ciudad Madero, Tamaulipas Sheinbaum closed her Tamaulipas tour inaugurating the Ciudad Madero IMSS Bienestar General Hospital — the 32nd hospital opened since she took office. She laid out the path to a Universal Health Service: anyone will be able to be treated at IMSS, ISSSTE or IMSS Bienestar, whichever is closest, regardless of affiliation.
📸 Inauguración del Hospital General ISSSTE — Tampico, Tamaulipas, 15 de agosto de 2026

🇲🇽📰 MEXICO THIS WEEKEND — AUG 15–16 · Tamaulipas tour: Sheinbaum closed a four-city swing — Reynosa, Matamoros, Ciudad Victoria, Tampico — delivering Bienestar housing (84,000+ families statewide via FOVISSSTE/Conavi), Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro job placements, and the new ISSSTE General Hospital in Tampico. · "A visa does not define a person": her line in Tampico, to loud cheers — conviction in sovereignty, and that in Mexico no one outranks the people. · Universal Health Service: nationwide registration for the Servicio Universal de Salud credential ran Aug 10–15, reopening sign-up for ages 30–64 tied to the Pensión Bienestar.

🇲🇽🌎 "Without sovereignty, they would have imposed the privatization of health care from abroad." "A gallbladder surgery at market price costs about 150,000 pesos. A heart surgery, 700,000. A spine surgery, 600,000. Without sovereignty, they probably would have imposed health privatization from the outside." — Martí Batres, ISSSTE director, in Tampico Batres spoke at the inauguration of the ISSSTE General Hospital in Tampico, which opens with 35 specialties and adds imaging, surgery, chemotherapy and a blood bank in the coming weeks.

🇲🇽🏥 36 neoliberal years: 1,664 ISSSTE beds. The 4T: over 2,000 in two terms. "In 36 years the ISSSTE grew by barely a thousand beds — 1,600 beds. But the population grew, the number of state workers grew, and the hospitals stayed the same." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Tampico The new Tampico hospital replaces the old ISSSTE unit: from 103 to 250 beds, 20 to 37 consult rooms, a pharmacy 10 times larger. ISSSTE director Martí Batres: six neoliberal terms built 1,664 beds; the Fourth Transformation will add more than 2,000.

🇲🇽✊ Health care is a right, not a privilege. "The problem is when private replaces public — then access to health becomes a privilege, not a right. Because it's for those who have money, not for those who have the least." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Tampico Sheinbaum inaugurated the new ISSSTE General Hospital in Tampico, Tamaulipas: 250 beds, 37 specialty consult rooms, MRI, hemodynamics and dialysis — free, public care.
banner: "HEALTH IS A RIGHT, NOT A PRIVILEGE"
